title: Chemical Reactions and Equations: Chapter Introduction
summary: A burning magnesium ribbon leaves only white powder: the same atoms in a new arrangement. How to spot a reaction, write and balance its equation, and name its type.

notes.title: 00 – Chemical Reactions and Equations: Chapter Introduction

keyPoints: Burning magnesium gives magnesium oxide: **2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO**. The atoms are the same, only rearranged.
Signs of a reaction: **gas** given off, **colour** change, **temperature** change, **precipitate** formed (or a change of state).
A **balanced** equation has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides (law of conservation of mass).
Types: **combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, redox**. Everyday effects: **corrosion** (rusting) and **rancidity** (chips packets are flushed with nitrogen).
